title: SC$^\sharp$: superconductivity intertwined with topological order
authors: Zhi-Qiang Gao, Yan-Qi Wang, Hui Yang, Zhaoyu Han, Ashvin Vishwanath
abstract: Superconductivity and intrinsic topological order can intertwine in ways that go beyond simple coexistence. Here we develop a classification framework for (2+1)D gapped superconductors with condensate charge $2ne$. By focusing on the topological properties of superconducting vortices, we precisely characterize this interplay. We obtain a classification with increasing levels of intertwinement, from the well known invertible superconductors without topological order, to untwisted and twisted SC$^\ast$, and finally to SC$^{\sharp}$. Our main finding is the family SC$^{\sharp}$, in which the elementary vortex carrying $h/(2ne)$ flux cannot be factorized into an invertible superconductor vortex dressed by bulk anyons, and every elementary vortex is necessarily non-Abelian. For such phases, we also obtain no-go results: the elementary vortex sector has quantum dimension at least $\sqrt{6}$ and cannot satisfy Fibonacci fusion rules. We develop a systematic algebraic framework to obtain all these superconducting phases through anyon condensation, allowing us to construct several infinite families of examples and make connections to anyon superconductivity. Finally, we introduce primitive SC$^\sharp$ phases for which factorization of every nontrivial vortex sector is obstructed, and argue that they cannot arise by disordering the relative phases of lower-charge superconducting condensates. Our classification scheme based on vortex properties allows us to uncover new distinctions between topologically ordered superconductors and constrain how they can be realized.
summary: This paper classifies superconducting phases based on how strongly superconductivity intertwines with intrinsic topological order in 2D materials. The authors introduce the SC^sharp phase, which is defined by non-factorizable, non-Abelian vortex excitations. This work provides a powerful topological diagnostic tool to distinguish between different types of exotic superconducting states.
main_problem: To develop a comprehensive classification framework for (2+1)D gapped superconductors that precisely characterizes the interplay between superconductivity and intrinsic topological order.
main_result: The authors introduce the class SC^sharp, characterized by elementary vortices that cannot be factorized into simple superconducting and topological components, implying a fundamentally non-Abelian nature.
method: The classification relies on analyzing the topological properties of superconducting vortices using an algebraic framework involving modular tensor categories.
model_or_system: The system studied is a (2+1)D gapped superconductor with a condensate charge of 2ne, analyzed through the lens of anyon physics and topological field theory.
key_observables: Topological properties of superconducting vortices, quantum dimension of the elementary vortex sector, and fusion rules.
important_parameters: Condensate charge (2ne), flux quanta (h/(2ne)), and the level of intertwinement between SC and TO.
main_assumptions: The classification is argued to be exhaustive by relating all SC phases to anyon condensation from a parent UMTC.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the classification scheme, grading the intertwinement between SC and TO based on vortex properties.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining a hierarchy of superconducting phases: invertible SC $	o$ SC* $	o$ Twisted SC* $	o$ SC^sharp $	o$ Primitive SC^sharp, with each step defined by increasingly restrictive conditions on vortex factorization.
why_interesting: The deep connection between superconductivity, topological order, and non-Abelian anyons provides a rich theoretical playground for understanding emergent quantum phases in condensed matter systems.
